prerequisites: Previous mathematics background at the level of high school Mathematics I and II, with a scientific-technological orientation
Knowledge of solving systems of linear equations and basic concepts related to matrix theory

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering.

Aptitude to apply knowledge on: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.

Has the aptitude to apply acquired knowledge on the following topics of Linear Algebra and Geometry: Matrix algebra; systems of linear equations and basic iterative methods for their resolution; vector spaces; linear applications; matrix diagonalization; inner product spaces; differential geometry.
Solves mathematical problems that may arise in Engineering.
Knows how to use numerical methods and mathematical software in solving some mathematical problems.
Has proficiency in handling mathematical language; in particular, symbolic and formal language.
Knows the reflective use of symbolic and numerical calculation tools.
Possesses skills characteristic of scientific-mathematical thinking, which allow asking and answering mathematical questions, correctly and rigorously.

syllabus_topics: Systems of linear equations and numerical methods.
Euclidean geometry: inner product, orthogonalization and applications.
Differential geometry: curves in space, Frenet frame, representation of plane curves.
assessment_rules: To pass the theoretical-practical exam, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required. If the score is less than 4, this will be the final grade for the course, regardless of the computer lab practice grade. The computer lab practice grade is retained for both official calls of the academic year, but students may opt to renounce it and take a corresponding test in the global exam. The global exam consists of a written exam for both parts (Theoretical-practical and Practices) in each official call, also requiring a minimum of 4 points out of 10 in the theoretical-practical part.
